items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Edgar Haynes James was the only one that had a few drops in his glass and he was arrested... We went to the jail to see Edgar the next day... leave Edgar some money

ctx.x: quite a bit to drink before we left Bluefield, I was as sober as a teetotaler and so tired that the moment I entered my room in the hotel, and as soon as I got my clothes off and hit the hay, I was asleep before anyone could say Jack Rabbit and it was late afternoon when I awakened.

We only had those two dances in West Virginia and stayed in Charleston after coming from Bluefield to rest before hitting the road for Cincinnati. After having slept most of the day, a few of us met in a house where moonshine whisky was sold and we were having a grand time until suddenly there was a noise in the kitchen and in came some men (white) with revolvers flashing and told everyone in the room not to move. We all had glasses in front of us, but Edgar Haynes James was the only one that had a few drops in…

We went to the jail to see Edgar the next day before we left for Cincinnati and we were told that Edgar's trial would not be held for a week. So we had to go in our pockets to leave Edgar some money so that he would have enough to pay his fine and come back to Cincinnati when he was freed. The only profit that I received from my first trip out of Cincinnati with the Clarence Page orchestra was the ride in the car for my first visit to the state of West Virginia.
